source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check how many type of power action can do via WebUI.
EX: power cycle / power reset / cold and warm reboot / NMI
2. Using each one of them once.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. All power action can normally set.
2. System will do a correct action.
EX: If use normal power cycle, then system will reboot by a normal process.
if use immediately power cycle, then system will shut down immediately and power on.
3. No Device will lost after power action under OS.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power off 2>&1; sleep 10; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power on 2>&1; sleep 30; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis power status 2>&1
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: exercise the server power operations (off/on/cycle) via ipmitool and return the power-state result of each action so user confirms all power actions work.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: state-changing: powers the SUT off/on; ensure no jobs are running and confirm with the user before powering off.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL notices power risk but its off/sleep/on/status chain tests neither the source WebUI nor the enumerated action set, conflates graceful and immediate semantics, omits NMI/reset evidence, exposes credentials and cannot prove OS shutdown integrity or device preservation.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires discovery of supported actions, one approved action at a time, workload drain, bounded recovery and pre/post OS/device comparison. V3.1 additionally requires a semantic map for every UI label and keeps NMI crash/dump evidence distinct from power-state evidence.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 914/2291 accepts the off/on command conditionally but does not establish WebUI coverage, action-specific semantics, NMI dump handling, graceful shutdown markers, device inventory scope, recovery deadlines or stop-on-first-failure behavior.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Simple power-on/off, AC/DC cycle, BMC reboot, host reboot and next-boot override cases do not establish this WebUI action matrix. NMI is an interrupt/fault-injection path, not proof of a power cycle.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1076, Wistron-BMC-00205-V003 or 229a9220edcaa0ab draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves WebUI as the original method; ED-34 treats supported labels/semantics and timing as Project inputs; ED-35 requires actual functional action and post-state coverage rather than read-only status; ED-38 requires point-of-action approval, one action, no automatic retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify every Project-supported BMC WebUI server power action executes its documented graceful, immediate, reset, cycle, reboot or NMI semantics exactly once and returns the SUT to the expected state without losing applicable OS-visible devices.
original_method: Inventory the actual WebUI power-action labels and map each to vendor semantics, establish a drained dedicated-host baseline, then for one approved action at a time capture the request/audit event, independently observe OS shutdown/reset/NMI and chassis transitions, wait within action-specific limits, verify recovery and compare complete applicable device inventory before proceeding.
manual_activity: An engineer supplies the authoritative action matrix and expected transition for each UI label, drains/approves the host and confirms every individual action. A human may need to click the source WebUI control and supervise console/recovery, especially for NMI or immediate-off. Automation can baseline, monitor and compare states, but cannot authorize the sequence or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT/host identity, firmware/WebUI/BIOS/OS versions and initial power/runtime state
Supported WebUI action list with exact graceful/immediate/reset/cycle/warm/cold/NMI semantics and expected final state
Dedicated-host maintenance approval and evidence that jobs, users, storage/RAID, firmware work and dependent services are drained
Action-specific audit/power/OS/console event mapping, timing limits and recovery criteria
Complete applicable pre/post device inventory definition including storage, network, PCIe/GPU and services
NMI crash/dump expectation and collection path where NMI is supported
Independent console/OOB recovery and owner escalation for hang, boot failure, filesystem/device loss or wrong action
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC/SEL, OS journal, crash, storage or audit logs; preserve the pre-action baseline and first-failure evidence.
Verify the exact target and UI label immediately before each action. Do not translate a WebUI action to ipmitool/Redfish without documented semantics and coverage tracking.
Do not run on an active workload or combine off/on/reset/cycle/NMI into a chain. Obtain separate point-of-action approval and stable post-state for every action.
Treat NMI separately: confirm crash-kernel/dump policy and expected OS behavior; do not assume it powers or reboots the host.
Use bounded transition/recovery observations, not fixed sleeps or chassis status alone. Stop on wrong semantics, timeout, filesystem errors or missing devices.
Do not automatically recover with another reset/power command or continue the matrix after failure; preserve evidence and invoke the approved console/recovery plan.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, WebUI action/semantic map, drained-host evidence, complete baseline, action-specific expected state, approval and recovery before presenting one action.
After human WebUI interaction or approved equivalent, correlate UI/audit request with independent host, console, OS and chassis transitions using bounded polling.
After stabilization, collect action-specific logs and compare complete applicable device/service inventory and persistent boot/power settings with baseline before any next action.
Stop without log clear, combined actions, insecure credentials, fixed-sleep acceptance, automatic retry/matrix continuation or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the supported WebUI action list and exact semantics/final state for every label, including NMI and graceful versus immediate variants.
Approve workload drain, each point-of-action, action-specific timing, dump/recovery and device-inventory acceptance.
Review each action's request, transitions, logs and post-state independently and issue formal verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Materially incomplete: off then on is not the source's WebUI matrix, cannot demonstrate graceful versus immediate behavior, reset/cycle/warm/cold/NMI, and final power status cannot prove OS or device integrity. It also exposes the password and uses fixed delays.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact approved WebUI action once per checkpoint. If an API/ipmitool override is approved, record method and semantic equivalence; monitor action-specific OS/console/chassis evidence and compare full post-state before proceeding.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The WebUI inventory, examples power cycle/power reset/cold-warm reboot/NMI, once-per-action instruction, normal-versus-immediate examples, no-device-loss Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek command/risk and 10/10-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not treat those estimates as universal deadlines.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a version-specific WebUI action matrix and execute each action as an isolated approved experiment with independent transition observation, action-specific recovery and complete pre/post device comparison.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC WebUI and SUT firmware/OS with dedicated maintenance and independent console recovery.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/WebUI schema, BIOS/UEFI, OS/kernel, crash/dump, storage/network/GPU drivers and monitoring versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: BMC vendor power-action semantics, Project maintenance/recovery policy, OS shutdown/crash-dump and device-enumeration acceptance specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes every UI action and expected transition measurable, separates NMI, adds workload drain, bounded recovery and device integrity while retaining the original WebUI scope.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: ipmitool off/on does not prove WebUI controls or other actions; chassis status does not prove graceful shutdown, NMI handling or device preservation; one action cannot stand in for the matrix.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Action semantics, drained host, timings, inventory, recovery and individual approvals.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Power interruption or NMI can corrupt data, lose crash evidence or strand the host; labels may map differently across firmware; repeated actions compound thermal/storage and availability risk.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use IPMI, Redfish or a vendor tool only if the original WebUI control, actual operation, reason, engineer approval, semantic equivalence and uncovered UI coverage are recorded per action. Passing off/on cannot claim reset, cycle, graceful shutdown, warm/cold reboot or NMI. Unsupported actions need authoritative N/A evidence.
expected_evidence: Target and version identity, approved action/semantic matrix, maintenance/workload-drain record, initial power/OS/device/boot-policy baseline and recovery readiness
Per-action WebUI screenshots/audit or approved override mapping, point-of-action approval and exact request timestamp
Independent console/host/chassis transition timeline with graceful shutdown, reset/cycle or NMI/crash-dump markers as applicable
Bounded management/host recovery plus complete pre/post OS device/service/log comparison and persistent-setting check
Stop/recovery disposition, preserved first-failure evidence, no automatic retry, explicit method coverage and engineer-owned per-action verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently request the supported server-power action matrix and correct action-specific behavior. Examples use imprecise vendor-neutral labels, but exact labels and semantics are discoverable Project inputs rather than irreconcilable source purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The power-action matrix purpose and original WebUI path are clear. Project/vendor documentation can define supported actions, semantics, timing and recovery, so missing data makes execution pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but rejects the chained off/on/fixed-sleep shortcut and adds full UI action, NMI, OS/device and stop-on-failure coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification and strengthens semantic mapping, NMI-specific evidence, per-action stable-state gate and method-specific coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists sanity with isolated action experiments and action-specific proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps simple power and boot-option variants separate from this supported WebUI matrix.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an off/on pair and final power status from being reported as proof of graceful, immediate, reset, cycle, warm/cold and NMI behavior or of post-action device preservation.
independent_technical_reasoning: Power-control labels describe different state machines: graceful actions require OS shutdown evidence, immediate actions intentionally bypass it, reset/cycle differ in power removal, and NMI is an interrupt whose success may be a dump rather than a power transition. Because the source also requires no device loss, every action needs an independent baseline, exact semantic expectation, transition evidence and complete post-recovery inventory before the matrix can continue.
